brief.situation: 13:05 in the emergency department. You are the nurse who takes Ms. Lindqvist, 38, from triage into a monitored room. A bee stung her hand at a picnic 15 minutes ago; her friend drove her in.
handover: Triage: hives over her chest and arms, lips swelling, 'my throat feels tight', wheeze. Blood pressure 88/54, heart rate 118. ESI 1.

The department's anaphylaxis standing order: epinephrine IM in the mid-outer thigh at the order's adult dose, repeated after 5 minutes if airway, breathing or circulation problems persist; supine with legs raised, or semi-recumbent if breathing is easier, and no standing or sudden posture changes; oxygen; two IVs and a crystalloid bolus for hypotension; antihistamine and corticosteroid only after epinephrine.
The emergency physician is at the next bed and will come when called.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Treatments act over minutes, and the order matters. Reassess after each one.
Partway through you are asked to write what you think is happening. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: What is happening to Ms. Lindqvist, and in what order do you treat it?

parts.label: What
parts.criteria: Anaphylaxis: skin and lips, throat tightness and wheeze, hypotension, minutes after a sting.
parts.modelAnswer: Hives, swelling lips, a tight throat with wheeze and a blood pressure of 88 minutes after a sting: anaphylaxis with airway and circulation involved.

parts.label: In what order
parts.criteria: IM epinephrine first, mid-outer thigh, repeated after 5 minutes if problems persist; flat with legs up, never standing; oxygen; IV fluid for hypotension; antihistamine and steroid only after; the physician now.
parts.modelAnswer: Epinephrine IM in the thigh first, and again in 5 minutes if she is still hypotensive or wheezy. Lay her down with legs up and keep her there. Oxygen, two IVs and a bolus. The antihistamine and steroid come after. Physician to the bedside now.

collapse.headline: Collapse on standing
collapse.body: In anaphylaxis, keep her lying down with legs raised, or sitting slightly up if breathing needs it. Standing can empty the heart.

obstruction.headline: Airway lost
obstruction.body: Epinephrine IM is the treatment, first and early, repeated after 5 minutes if problems persist. An antihistamine does not treat airway or circulation.

stable.headline: Right order
stable.body: Epinephrine first and repeated on time, flat with legs up, fluid, then the adjuncts. That is the expert path.

stableLate.headline: Stabilizing, with gaps
stableLate.body: Check the time to the first dose, whether it was repeated at 5 minutes, her posture and whether the adjuncts came first.

scoring.modelReasoning: Skin and lip swelling, throat tightness with wheeze and hypotension minutes after a sting is anaphylaxis. Epinephrine IM in the mid-outer thigh comes first, repeated after 5 minutes while airway, breathing or circulation problems persist. She lies flat with legs raised, or semi-recumbent for breathing, and never stands. Oxygen, IV access and fluid for the hypotension; antihistamine and steroid only after epinephrine; the physician to the bedside.

firstQ.ask: While you assess: what treats the airway and circulation in anaphylaxis?
firstQ.explain: Epinephrine IM in the anterolateral thigh is the primary treatment; antihistamines do not treat airway, breathing or circulation problems.
